title: Specified open and closed normalization of ordinary etale compact supports
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $j:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion and let $c:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes. Assume the morphisms are separated of finite type and have chosen compactifications. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], extension by zero $j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], direct image $c_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and compact-support candidates [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. The functor $c_*$ on these module sheaves is exact. Write $Dj_!$ and $Dc_*$ for degreewise descent of the exact sheaf functors to the derived categories. For every integer $m$, both functors preserve complexes with cohomology zero below $m$, and naturally $\mathcal H^q(Dj_!H)=j_!\mathcal H^q(H)$ and $\mathcal H^q(Dc_*L)=c_*\mathcal H^q(L)$. On bounded-below inputs there are natural isomorphisms $$n_j:Rj_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Dj_!,\qquad n_c:Rc_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Dc_*.$$ These are the specified normalizations: compare the chosen compactification to $(j,\mathrm{id}_T)$ or $(\mathrm{id}_Z,c)$ using the canonical proper-refinement identifications [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], then use $R\mathrm{id}_*=\mathrm{id}$ for the open factor, respectively $D\mathrm{id}_!=\mathrm{id}$ and the exact-functor comparison $Rc_*\cong Dc_*$ for the closed factor. The comparisons commute with morphisms of bounded-below inputs and with the canonical changes of chosen compactification. Each is an isomorphism in the ambient unbounded category; no compactification comparison is asserted here on an unbounded input.

proof.text: The closed immersion $c$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Hence its direct image on abelian étale sheaves is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]. The module direct image is additive and commutes with forgetting the $A$-module structure by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. For a short exact sequence of $A_Z$-module sheaves, forget the action, apply the abelian direct image, and obtain a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves. The forgetful functor preserves kernels and cokernels and is faithful by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; thus it reflects zero objects (the identity of an object with zero underlying sheaf is zero), and therefore reflects exactness by testing the kernel modulo the image. The resulting module sequence is short exact. This proves exactness of $c_*$ on ordinary étale module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero); module transfer: sites-modules.tex Tags 03DA/03DB (lemma-abelian, lemma-limits-colimits)

proof.text: For the open immersion, [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] gives exactness of $j_!$ on $A$-module sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to this functor and to the exact $c_*$ from step 1. Their termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and descend to the unbounded derived functors $Dj_!$ and $Dc_*$, with $Dj_!Q_W\cong Q_T C(j_!)$ and $Dc_*Q_Z\cong Q_T C(c_*)$, where $C$ denotes termwise application and $Q$ denotes localization. No lower cohomological bound is required for these two descents.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] to $j_!$ and $c_*$. It gives the natural isomorphisms $\mathcal H^q(Dj_!H)\cong j_!\mathcal H^q(H)$ and $\mathcal H^q(Dc_*L)\cong c_*\mathcal H^q(L)$ on the unbounded categories. If the input cohomology vanishes in degrees $q<m$, the right sides vanish there because an additive functor sends the zero object to zero. Thus the same integer $m$ works after either functor; in particular bounded-below inputs remain bounded below.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), termwise computation and its cohomology consequence

proof.text: The identity direct image is canonically the identity: in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] the fibre product $V\times_T T$ is canonically $V$, with the same restriction maps. The identity open extension is also the identity: in [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] every object factors uniquely through the identity, so its extension presheaf is the original sheaf. Its sheafification is canonically itself by the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]: the map back extending the identity and the sheafification map are inverse by uniqueness. These identifications are natural. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], their termwise identifications descend uniquely to $D\mathrm{id}_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $D\mathrm{id}_!\cong\mathrm{id}$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identifies the right derived functor of the exact identity direct image with its termwise descent, giving the specified $R\mathrm{id}_*\cong\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), identity case; extension by zero as in etale-cohomology.tex equation-j-p-shriek

proof.text: Use the compactifications $b_j=(j,\mathrm{id}_T)$ and $b_c=(\mathrm{id}_Z,c)$. The former has proper second factor since an identity is separated, finite type and universally closed; the latter has proper second factor by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Their candidates, by [def-amb-etale-compact-support], are $R\mathrm{id}_{T,*}Dj_!$ and $Rc_*D\mathrm{id}_{Z,!}$. Step 4 supplies a natural isomorphism $e_j:Rj_!^{b_j}\xrightarrow{\sim}Dj_!$. For the closed case apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] to the exact module functor $c_*$ of step 1: the canonical comparison $Dc_*\to Rc_*$ is invertible on every complex. Its inverse, together with $D\mathrm{id}_{Z,!}\cong\mathrm{id}$ from step 4, supplies $e_c:Rc_!^{b_c}\xrightarrow{\sim}Dc_*$. These are precisely the termwise and identity normalizations.

For $a=j$ or $a=c$, let $d$ be its chosen compactification and let $\rho_{d,b_a}:Ra_!^d\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_!^{b_a}$ be the canonical comparison on bounded-below inputs from [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Define $n_a^d=e_a\circ\rho_{d,b_a}$. The hypotheses of that comparison hold: the coefficient ring is finite, both schemes are Noetherian, and the morphism is separated, finite type and compactifiable by assumption. Step 3 ensures that the exact-factor outputs needed in the trivial-compactification computations remain bounded below. Each component of $n_a^d$ is a composite of isomorphisms in the ambient unbounded derived category, since the candidates of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] are functors into that category. This proves the claimed isomorphisms for every bounded-below input.

source.place: Tag 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined), canonical comparisons through common refinements

proof.text: Every constituent of $n_a^d$ is natural, so for a morphism $u:H\to H'$ of bounded-below inputs its square is $D_a(u)\,n_{a,H}^d=n_{a,H'}^d\,Ra_!^d(u)$, where $D_j=Dj_!$ and $D_c=Dc_*$. For another chosen compactification $d'$, the cocycle identity in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] gives $\rho_{d',b_a}\rho_{d,d'}=\rho_{d,b_a}$; hence $n_a^{d'}\rho_{d,d'}=e_a\rho_{d',b_a}\rho_{d,d'}=e_a\rho_{d,b_a}=n_a^d$. This is compatibility with changing compactifications, including identities and refinements. Only bounded-below inputs were used in these equations.

tool_uses.why: Finite direct-image exactness supplies abelian etale closed-pushforward exactness; the unit has no abelian exactness theorem.
Its compatibility with forgetting scalar actions transfers the abelian computation to constant modules; the unit supplies no such module interface.
Faithful exact forgetful functors detect exactness of the module sequence; this is generic ringed-site algebra.
Exact open extension is required for the open normalization; this is an ordinary etale-site tool, not a replacement of the unit route.
Generic cohomology comparison for exact functors proves the precise lower-bound clause; the unit gives no abstract derived-functor statement.

lean.statement: theorem etaleImmersionShriekNormalization (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] {W Z T : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian W] [IsNoetherian Z] [IsNoetherian T] (j : W ⟶ T) [IsOpenImmersion j] (c : Z ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion c] (dj : Compactification j) (dc : Compactification c) : (PreservesFiniteLimits (lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c) ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits (lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c)) ∧ (∀ (m : ℤ) (H : DerivedCategoryModule A W), H.IsGE m → ((openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).mapDerivedCategory.obj H).IsGE m) ∧ (∀ (m : ℤ) (L : DerivedCategoryModule A Z), L.IsGE m → ((lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c).mapDerivedCategory.obj L).IsGE m) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, Nonempty ((openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q ≅ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q ⋙ openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j)) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, Nonempty ((lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q ≅ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q ⋙ lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c)) ∧ (∀ dj' : Compactification j, rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusιIso A dj dj' ≪≫ etaleOpenCompactSupportNormalization A j dj' = etaleOpenCompactSupportNormalization A j dj) ∧ (∀ dc' : Compactification c, rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusιIso A dc dc' ≪≫ etaleClosedCompactSupportNormalization A c dc' = etaleClosedCompactSupportNormalization A c dc)
